repairs.title: Team overview shows zero or inflated event counts
repairs.scope: Read-only team-event overview statistics; individual-event statistics retain their own registration source.
repairs.symptoms: Team rosters exist but the overview shows zero entries or paid players, inflated teams or players, or no match progress.
repairs.cause: Individual registration counts were reused for team operations; region-wide teams were not event scoped, roster mirrors and empty places were counted as players, and individual fixtures supplied team match progress.
repairs.fix: Use TeamEventOverviewStats through EventOperationsService and reuse that snapshot in the overview. Resolve owned teams through EventTeamScope; count occupied profile places or authoritative imported identities once. Imported payment can live on an exact team/rank/profile TeamPlayer mirror. Count event TeamPaymentOrder checkout, paid-withdrawal and refund states separately; use completed TeamRubberResultService outcomes for team match progress. Keep draw totals exact while readiness remains bounded.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-04 isolated SQLite TeamEventOverviewStatsTest, EventOperationsPendingCheckoutTest and EventOverviewPresentationTest passed 8 tests and 83 assertions, covering shared/exclusive regions, empty places, imported mirrors, order states, completed versus partial results, event authorization and exact draw totals. AssistantRepairLibraryTest passed 3 tests and 150 assertions. Route registration, Blade compilation and debug-call checks passed. Browser, MySQL and production behavior remain unverified.
repairs.limits: Guide only; aggregation does not modify rosters, orders, wallets, payments, refunds, fixtures or publication. Ambiguous shared-region legacy teams need canonical ownership evidence rather than guessed attribution. Existing overview authorization and pending-checkout audience limits remain in force. Deployment requires separate authorization.

repairs.title: Paid team replacement blocked or remains unpaid after refund funding
repairs.scope: Standard paid roster replacements by a super user; full payment carry-over, wallet refunds, refund-funded replacements and refund waivers.
repairs.symptoms: Saving a replacement rejects its refund after the deadline, reports Withdrawals are currently disabled, or leaves a same-price replacement unpaid because net refund funding deducted the withdrawal fee.
repairs.cause: The refund deadline and global withdrawal closure are independent guards. Net refund funding deducts the normal fee and can leave a shortfall. Full payment carry-over requires a separate explicit choice.
repairs.fix: Choose Move full payment to replacement for explicit fee-free carry-over, or Use refund toward replacement player for net funding with the normal withdrawal fee. Only the transfer action derives canonical fee_mode full server-side. The original payer funds a separate replacement checkout capped at current entry plus regional fee; full coverage finalizes payment, excess stays in their wallet and a genuine higher-price shortfall remains payable. Separately confirm closure and deadline overrides when applicable and give a reason. Canonical review, fingerprint, confirmation and audit retain source history, managed-selection guards, atomic rollback and stale-state checks. Public settings stay unchanged. See docs/refund-funded-team-replacements.md.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-04 isolated SQLite AdminTeamWithdrawalTest and RegionalRosterTest passed 57 tests and 737 assertions after adding explicit full-payment carry-over. Coverage includes equal/lower/higher replacement entry and regional fees, hybrid/imported settlement, exact zero-fee credit, original payer/history, replay counts, managed-selection and role/event denial, rollback, separate closure/deadline consent and forged fee_mode on ordinary actions. PHP lint, route registration, Blade compilation, debug-call scan and diff checks passed. Independent quality and financial reviews found no issues. MySQL, browser execution of the new option and production mutation remain unverified; Separate correction verification passed 67 affected tests and 997 assertions, including 10 correction tests and 250 assertions. The correction preview passed against the reviewed remote state without applying financial changes; final execution requires explicit supervised apply. Broader Feature run stopped after 140 tests and 1121 assertions at the unrelated AllAgeHistoricalPresentationTest.php:25 array-offset error.
repairs.limits: Explicit super-user confirmation is required. Ordinary refunds and net-funded replacements retain the normal fee; only the explicit full-payment option waives it. This does not bypass competition or selection guards, rewrite original payment history, automatically reconcile an already-created replacement, or authorize live refunds or deployment. For an already refunded replacement, the separate finance:correct-team-replacement preview/apply workflow requires exact unused refund and closed checkout evidence, compensates the original credit, preserves receipt/history and restores beneficiary coverage. Deploy its future-refund guards together; see the domain documentation and TeamReplacementPaymentCorrectionTest. A refund waiver returns no money and cannot combine with a deadline override; closure consent remains required when disabled. Ordinary withdrawal endpoints do not accept the replacement closure override.

repairs.title: Feed-in bracket omits unplayed bye paths
repairs.scope: Display of fixed 16/32-slot Feed-in Monrad templates in browser, print and PDF; no fixture generation or stored graph changes.
repairs.symptoms: An opening feed-in column has a blank branch and the later match receives an earlier main-draw loser directly, hiding that player's bye advance.
repairs.cause: Canonical compilation correctly collapses unplayed bye matches, but the presentation previously restored only main-draw bye paths.
repairs.fix: Project collapsed feed-in paths through withFeedInByes and FlexibleMonradFeedInDisplay. Match saved source signatures before expanding; retain incompatible historical topology unchanged. Show unnumbered Bye cards and original feeder labels, keeping unresolved losers pending and showing resolved losers only after a known winner. Do not persist synthetic cards or add them to scheduling/result entry. See DK-06 in docs/draw-knowledge/catalogue.md.

repairs.title: Knockout match numbers jump between rounds

repairs.cause: FlexibleMonradService assigned numbers in the compiler's depth-first node insertion order.
repairs.fix: Use FlexibleMonradCompiler::fixtureOrder during new generation: progression stage first, main draw then highest placement bands, preserving topology order within each band. repairs.title: Feed-in byes collapse into one branch
repairs.scope: Individual 16- and 32-slot Feed-in Monrad generation across age groups; existing scored and published graphs are protected.
repairs.symptoms: Balanced main-draw byes leave both direct feed-in advances together, producing one large empty opening branch.

repairs.fix: Preserve absent main-path loser sources through adjacent opening pairs and the reversed next-round loser crossing. For size 32, pair survivors before ordered quarterfinal-loser entry. Collapse byes without canonical fixtures or invented losses. repairs.title: Director net payment leaves clothing deductions unreconciled
repairs.scope: Recording an already-paid full director settlement; registration funds and explicitly linked regional clothing only.
repairs.symptoms: The registration-only amount differs from the projected net payout because a linked clothing deficit must be withheld, or clothing payable must be included.
repairs.cause: A registration-only director payment does not create the corresponding clothing settlement evidence. Recording only the cash amount leaves a residual registration balance and the clothing deficit unchanged.
repairs.fix: Use the full outstanding balance option in Record payment to director. Review the server-derived registration balance, each linked clothing adjustment and actual net cash paid. Supply actual payment time and reference and confirm the already-paid amount. EventDirectorNetSettlementService atomically records the registration settlement and canonical linked clothing legs. A linked recovery is withholding, not a second cash receipt. Reject stale previews, ambiguous recipients, insufficient registration funds for deductions, and unsupported chronology; do not invent cross-region offsets.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-02 the focused net-settlement, reimbursement and payout-projection suite passed 24 tests with 230 assertions. DeploymentConfigTest passed 41 tests with 189 assertions. Checks are local; this record does not claim deployment or live verification.
repairs.limits: Clothing recording remains super-user only. Pending refunds remain reserved and may leave a clothing ledger balance even when currently payable amounts are zero. Requires the reviewed director settlement link migration. This guide executes no transfer, refund, publication or deployment and grants no new assistant action.

repairs.title: Category-copy request fails on natural wording and spoken leg numbers
repairs.scope: The event assistant's reviewed category-copy capability and background improvement notes; no live event mutation from this guide.
repairs.symptoms: The assistant asks for a special command format when a user says copy the source event categories to the destination, uses spoken leg numbers, or joins sponsor names with and.
repairs.cause: The earlier parser required categories from SOURCE to DESTINATION and split destination names at every and, including sponsor names.
repairs.fix: Support both explicit word orders, normalize spoken leg numbers and sponsor punctuation/order, and resolve the whole destination before splitting a real destination list. Keep bounded unique accessible matches and source year/place for inferred shorthand; show candidate names/IDs when ambiguous rather than guessing. Continue through the existing category preview and confirmed apply services. For a genuinely unsupported or unresolved instruction, use the actor-opted-in improvement handoff to save a deduplicated note for background review; a note does not execute the task or train a model.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-02 the independently run isolated assistant suite passed 128 tests and 986 assertions, including natural wording, ambiguity/year boundaries, preview/confirmation safety, automatic-note isolation and existing assistant flows. This is local test evidence, not live activation evidence.
repairs.limits: Exact event IDs/full names remain available. Typos are not silently guessed. Copying categories still needs the reviewed confirmation and preserves fee, authorization, stale-state and duplicate checks. Automatic forwarding is off by default and requires a separate exact actor allowlist; credential detection is heuristic and earlier conversation/draft fields are excluded. Background changes require tests and reviewed deployment before the live application learns the capability.

repairs.title: Upcoming team fixtures retain old roster names or playing order
repairs.scope: Source-aware team fixtures; authorised roster maintenance during open registration, without rewriting played history.

TeamParticipantHistoryService refreshes verified upcoming snapshot display names under the event lock while preserving source identity and link attestations. Open non-Trials team events save playing order through RosterOrderProtectionService without an extra confirmation; the same rollback checks still protect bookings, publication, results, started matches and unrelated teams. For ordinary non-Trials rosters without managed-selection or substitution-history restrictions, open-registration add, fill, remove, replacement and reserve controls remain available after generation, with atomic structural adaptation after the entire mutation. Structural changes may replan affected upcoming rubbers; order-only saves retain strict booking checks. Frozen started/scored fixtures and unrelated ties stay unchanged. Protected imported source rank/link/mirror mappings cannot be removed or remapped. Existing completed-match paid withdrawal/refund restrictions remain. See DK-26 for boundaries.

Coverage includes restored controls, structural adaptation, same-draw unrelated bookings, frozen started/scored records, imported identity preservation, paid refund rules, retries, closed registration and event isolation. These are local tests, not deployment or live evidence.

repairs.title: Past-event history refresh returns Too Many Requests after ordinary rating-page visits
repairs.scope: Authenticated player past-event rating-history refresh requests; no rating calculation or evidence-policy changes.
repairs.symptoms: The update-history form opens a bare 429 page even when the player history has not recently been refreshed.
repairs.cause: Unnamed numeric route throttles share the authenticated actor signature. Ordinary rating-page requests can consume the two-per-minute refresh allowance before the refresh controller runs.
repairs.fix: Authorize player-rating access first, then apply a dedicated actor-wide history-refresh limiter in PlayerEventRatingHistoryController. Keep two requests per minute across all players for that actor. Browser saturation redirects to the authorized history page with a retry message; JSON receives 429 with retry_after. Both include Retry-After and private no-store headers. Preserve the worker's per-player cooldown, request coalescing, lease and global builder lock.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-02 the focused isolated MySQL regression run passed 5 tests with 55 assertions, including unrelated-throttle isolation, retry expiry, actor-wide cross-player budgets, independent actors, denied-target precedence, existing entitlement checks and worker coalescing. This is local evidence only.

Coverage includes member filter tampering, ten-player bounds, one-player search selection, publication revocation, disconnected estimates, missing birth dates and administrative browsing. repairs.limits: This guide changes no live settings and restores no old policy automatically. Existing generic settings auditing was not absent; the repair adds coherent sanitized transaction-bound evidence. Do not globally disable model or request auditing.

repairs.title: Hidden dashboard tabs load expensive data or capped previews imply full totals
repairs.scope: Super Admin server-selected workspaces and their read-only financial/operational datasets.
repairs.symptoms: Opening Settings computes event ledgers or mail reports, queues stop at arbitrary caps, or financial totals change with the visible event page.
repairs.cause: One consolidated controller materialized every tab and client-only pagination hid incomplete server collections.
repairs.fix: Allowlist the selected workspace and use GET navigation. Load cheap shell aggregates separately; query and render only the selected detail panel. Pair conditional markup with guarded plugin resources and visible-table initialization. Server-paginate queues with stable order and retained tab/search/subtab context, and calculate true totals independently. Stream all selected-year events through the canonical ledger in bounded chunks while retaining only the displayed summary rows; never sum a single page as the year total.
repairs.verification: Eight workspace loading/pagination regressions and authenticated presentation/access checks passed within the local isolated MySQL dashboard suite on 2026-11-02. Nine executable JavaScript regressions cover save coordination, GET navigation and local subtab/audit initialization. No production timing benchmark is claimed.
repairs.limits: Read pagination does not authorize financial mutations, publication or broader access. Keep all Settings subpanes in their selected page's form to preserve bulk-save semantics. Independent refund model paginators must retain their companion page context.

repairs.title: Saved pathway badge has no highlighted competition while an update is pending
repairs.scope: Player Plus personal pathway snapshot; saved comparable standard-ball rating positioning only.
repairs.symptoms: A saved numeric badge is visible but none of Wilson B, Wilson A or TSA is highlighted when progression is not assessed.
repairs.cause: The visual current position used suggestedCompetition, which correctly becomes unavailable when the freshness assessment is pending.
repairs.fix: Use PlayerPathwayService currentCompetition to position the latest saved comparable nonlocal standard-ball score against configured cutoffs. Render the current card with aria-current and latest saved badge wording. Keep suggestedCompetition, assessed and readiness subject to freshness. Retain matching player, publication validation, entitlement and comparability gates. Use the shared loading modal on pathway navigation with timeout and pageshow cleanup.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-03 local focused PHP checks passed 34 tests and 500 assertions; independent frontend checks passed seven tests. Coverage includes stale saved positioning, exactly one highlighted card, cutoff boundaries, invalid scores, local estimates, player mismatch and revoked evidence. Synthetic browser checks passed loading success/failure and navigation at 390/1440 pixels. No production verification.
repairs.limits: Saved position is not a fresh progression recommendation or event eligibility. No rating recalculation, publication, ownership change or production action is authorized by this guide.

repairs.title: Regional roster fails to load after team fixtures are generated
repairs.scope: Players roster fragments with automatic playing-order controls for imported teams containing linked player profiles.
repairs.symptoms: The roster fragment returns HTTP 500 after fixture generation activates automatic playing-order controls; the local reproduction reports an attempt to read id on null.
repairs.cause: The players-region Blade reused the display fallback np as the imported roster identity. That fallback is intentionally null when a linked profile supplies the display name.
repairs.fix: In players-region automatic-order and name-form includes, resolve imported identity from slot->noProfile, matching the existing roster-action convention. Retain linked-profile display and rename restrictions, event/team authorization and expected-player stale-state checks. No roster or fixture data repair is needed.
repairs.verification: On 2026-11-04 the isolated SQLite regression failed with HTTP 500 before the fix. After the fix, AutomaticUpcomingFixtureUpdatesTest and TeamDrawAdaptationTest passed 29 tests and 166 assertions, including unchanged roster, fixture and participant attributes after rendering. Independent diff review found no issues.
repairs.limits: This guide does not authorize deployment, live data changes or bypassing roster protections. A generic roster error can have other causes; inspect the actual response and reproduce before applying this fix.

repairs.title: Team disciplines overlap or bulk age groups lose their scheduling boundaries
repairs.scope: Local event venue planning for team age groups, including manual assignments and legacy scheduling endpoints.
repairs.symptoms: Reverse singles, doubles or mixed begin before all earlier disciplines finish, or multiple age groups need one reviewed scheduling batch at their own assigned venues.
repairs.cause: Rubber sequence was a scheduling preference and programme section ordering controlled starts rather than complete age-wide discipline barriers.
repairs.fix: On supported team events, use the main scheduling page's visible venues and age-group programme. The unscoped page opens a bulk age draft; review the selected ages and each age's existing draw venues, courts and round cards before generating a preview. Event venue creation alone does not assign courts to an age. Canonical TeamDisciplineOrder dependencies enforce singles, reverse singles, doubles, then mixed independently per age and qualification stage. Retain unselected prerequisites and saved successors during partial replans, manual moves, removal and reset. Preview and save through the revision-checked service; publication remains separate. See DK-13 and DK-29 in docs/draw-knowledge/catalogue.md.
repairs.verification: Focused regression references cover distinct age venues, spare courts, unequal durations, strict completion, partial and manual bypasses, failed reset, composite programme cycles, invalid selection and source-to-placement dependencies. Frontend tests cover bulk selection and preservation of newer per-age edits during asynchronous saves. Current execution evidence belongs to the task handoff, not this coverage reference.
repairs.limits: Guide only; no automatic repair of saved or played schedules, venue reassignment, publication or production action. Composite cross-day round cards that conflict with all-singles-first must be rearranged; source qualification dependencies remain authoritative. Bulk daily windows and timing controls are shared while venue allocations remain per draw.
